Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment uses a specific chemical label (TMPP) to identify neo-N-termini generated by protease cleavage, alongside a glycoproteomics workflow using OpeRATOR protease and Byonic search. While TMPP is a label, it is used for site identification (neo-termini) rather than relative quantification, making 'Other' the most appropriate labeling strategy.

scope: The MUC2 N-and C-terminal recombinant proteins were expressed in CHO-K1 cells (CCL-61, ATCC) and purified from spent media by size-exclusion chromatography
EatA and the non-catalytic H134R mutant were cloned into a pBAD vector, expressed in E. coli and purified from concentrated spent LB media
bands of interest were excised from the gel and destained, proteins were reduced, alkylated, and digested using trypsin
The unmodified or GalNAc-modified 34-mer PTS3 peptide (JPT Peptide technologies) was dissolved in PBS and further diluted with 0.2% trifluoracetic acid to 2 µM for analysis by LC-MS/MS

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry analysis was performed on purified recombinant proteins (MUC2 fragments and EatA) and synthetic peptides, not on whole cell lysates or tissue extracts. Mixed species flag is true as both human recombinant proteins and E. coli proteins were analyzed.
